{{Short description|Czech-American mathematician}}
[[File:Václav Hlavatý (1894-1969).jpg|thumb|Václav portrait]]
'''Václav Hlavatý''' (27 January 1894 – 11 January 1969) was a noted [[Czech people|Czech]]-[[United States|American]] [[mathematician]], who wrote on the [[theory of relativity]] and corresponded extensively with [[Albert Einstein]] on the subject.<ref name=Indiana>{{Cite web |url=http://homepages.indiana.edu/011901/text/fastfacts.html |title=Indiana University fast facts |access-date=2008-08-19 |archive-date=2008-09-11 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080911113824/http://homepages.indiana.edu/011901/text/fastfacts.html |url-status=dead }}</ref>  In particular, Hlavatý solved some very difficult equations relating to Einstein's [[Unified field theory]], which was featured in the news media as one of the great scientific achievements of 1953.<ref name=JHopkins>{{Cite web |url=http://www.library.jhu.edu/collections/specialcollections/jhuxmlkineFind.body.html |title=Johns Hopkins Television Programs 1948–1960: Highlights of science for 1953 |access-date=2012-05-19 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20121211071244/http://www.library.jhu.edu/collections/specialcollections/jhuxmlkineFind.body.html |archive-date=2012-12-11 |url-status=dead }}</ref> Einstein himself was reported to have said that if anyone could solve the equations it would be Professor Hlavatý, which proved to be the case.<ref name=Czech1>[https://www.financnici.cz/vaclav-hlavaty Václav Hlavatý] Czech biography, citing the New York Herald Tribune</ref>

He was born in [[Louny]], [[Kingdom of Bohemia|Bohemia]] (now in the [[Czech Republic]]) and died in [[Bloomington, Indiana]]. He obtained his PhD in 1921 at the [[Charles University]] in [[Prague]]<ref name=Czech2>[http://www.mff.cuni.cz/toISO8859-2.en/fakulta/lib/hlavatdat.htm www.mff.cuni.cz] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120419105941/http://www.mff.cuni.cz/toISO8859-2.en/fakulta/lib/hlavatdat.htm |date=2012-04-19 }} Prof. Václav Hlavatý</ref><ref name=Hlavaty1928>V. Hlavatý (1928) ''Mathematische Zeitschrift'', Vol 28, No 1,  Bemerkung zur Arbeit von Herrn [[Tracy Yerkes Thomas|T. Y. Thomas]]</ref> and during [[World War II]] participated in the [[Prague uprising]],<ref name=Czech1 /> but his academic career was mainly at [[Indiana University]], which he joined in 1948, and where he became Professor, later Emeritus, of Mathematics. A special book of mathematical essays was published in his honour.<ref name=Hoffmann>[[Banesh Hoffmann|B. Hoffmann]] (ed.), ''Perspectives in Geometry and Relativity: Essays in Honor of Václav Hlavatý,'' Bloomington: Indiana UP, 1966.</ref> In 1958, he became the first President of the [[Czechoslovak Society of Arts and Sciences]]<ref name=LOC>[https://www.loc.gov/rr/european/imcz/ndl.html U.S. Library of Congress: ''The Czechs in America'']</ref> established in [[Washington DC]] by intellectuals of Czech and Slovak origin.

He was an Invited Speaker of the [[International Congress of Mathematicians|ICM]] in 1928 in Bologna and in 1936 in Oslo.

In 1931 he married Olga Neumannova, and they had a daughter, Olga.<ref name=Czech2 />
